chunks: Which of the favours of your Lord will then both of you deny?

key_terms.تُكَذِّبَانِ: you two will deny (dual verb form)
key_terms.رَبِّكُمَا: your Lord (dual form, addressing two groups)

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'Which of the favours of your Lord will you deny?' refer to in Surah Ar-Rahman?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this refrain serves as a cosmic interrogation directed at both the jinn and mankind, emphasizing the inescapable reality of divine favor. It underscores the theological principle that denial of God's blessings is a choice rather than an ignorance, linking human gratitude directly to the recognition of monotheism. The repetition highlights the cumulative weight of blessings, urging believers to reflect on the tangible signs of mercy in their daily lives.
